problem: CRIT-002's passThreshold text requires: 'a notify record (URL+screenshot fields) is written'. run.sh:223-224 does write those fields into notify.json ('{"draft_path": ..., "url": "pending-human-review", "screenshot": "pending-human-review"}'). But tests/test-prop6-modeA-draft.sh:16-17 only asserts that notify_path is non-empty and that the file exists ([ -n "$notify" ] && [ -f "$notify" ]) -- it never greps the file for the 'url' or 'screenshot' keys the passThreshold explicitly names. If a future edit dropped either field from notify.json's body, this test would still report PASS. This is a test-thoroughness gap, not an implementation defect (the fields genuinely exist today) -- non-blocking for this round.
fix: Add two assertions to tests/test-prop6-modeA-draft.sh after the notify-file-exists check: grep -q '"url"' "$notify" and grep -q '"screenshot"' "$notify", so the passThreshold's explicit field-presence claim is actually re-verifiable by the committed test suite.
